question: f0ffa0db0952's WATCHME (D7) fires on the heartbeat, cast 2026-09-22, before your 2026-09-30 ruling that all probes respond to events. Measured today: the wiring runs only when ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0 is absent (bin/cairn:153), and 7 of the 9 instance bins are symlinks to their class bins, so a new verb there is reachable with no wiring at all. CC recommends (a): drop the WATCHME (watchme 'none, because' citing the ruling) and keep the four-tooth proof as the whole guarantee. Or (b): keep a watch, fired by bin/cairn's dispatcher when 'cairn <dev> <verb>' misses while the class bin holds that verb, carrying a trouble. Which?
why_it_blocks: the WATCHME's trigger and consumer decide whether the build writes a probe at all; the ruling forbids the cast design and only you can pick its replacement
